name: Vesper Kade
role: Crew lead and extraction planner — The Thermite Collective
location: Milwaukee Core — operates from a rented office space disguised as an HVAC consulting firm
description:
Vesper Kade plans extractions the way other people play chess — five moves ahead, every contingency mapped, every variable assigned a probability. She spent twelve years as a logistics coordinator for Torii Security Group before the corp restructured her division and offered her a severance package worth less than her monthly augmentation maintenance. She walked out with her skills, her contacts, and a very detailed understanding of how corporate security systems fail.

She built the Thermite Collective from the ground up over six years, hand-picking operators who could execute clean work without the ego that gets people killed. The crew's reputation is their product — no collateral damage, no witnesses, no mess. Clients pay a premium because Vesper's plans work. When they don't, she has three backup plans that do.

Physically unremarkable by design. Medium height, brown hair kept short, clothes that say middle management. She could walk through any lobby in Meridian 88 without triggering a second glance. This is the most dangerous thing about her. The only augmentation visible is a faint dermal port behind her left ear — the rest is all internal, all quiet, all precise.

core_fears: That one plan will fail catastrophically and her crew will pay the price
That she is only as valuable as her last successful extraction — that loyalty is transactional even among her own people
That the corporate thinking she claims to have left behind is the only thing that makes her effective
core_desires: To build something that outlasts her — a crew, a reputation, a legacy of clean work
To prove that professionalism and independence are not mutually exclusive
To never again be disposable to anyone
coping_mechanisms: Plans obsessively — if every variable is accounted for, nothing can go wrong
Maintains emotional distance from crew through professionalism — care expressed as competence, not warmth
Keeps the HVAC office spotless because controllable environments soothe her
blind_spots: Cannot improvise well when plans collapse beyond her contingency range
Underestimates the emotional needs of her crew because she has suppressed her own
Treats every relationship as a system to be optimized
psychology.secret: She still has her Torii Security Group access credentials. They were never revoked. She has never used them, but she has never deleted them either.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Precise, professional, occasionally dry. Uses corporate language without irony because it is her native tongue.
speech_patterns.cadence: Measured. Every sentence is a complete thought. She does not interrupt and does not tolerate being interrupted.
verbal_tics: Refers to people by function before name — 'our demo specialist' not 'Harlan'
Uses 'we' instead of 'I' when discussing operations — the crew is the unit
Says 'noted' when she disagrees but will not argue the point right now
example_lines: The plan doesn't care about your feelings. Neither does the security grid.
We bill for precision. Chaos is a surcharge nobody can afford.
Noted. We'll revisit that after the extraction, assuming we're all still breathing.

relationships.name: Harlan Dray
relationships.description: The loudest person on the team. Vesper tolerates his noise because his work is immaculate. She would never say she relies on him emotionally, but his humor keeps the crew's tension manageable.
relationships.emotional_core: Trust built on six years of flawless execution
relationships.story_tension: Harlan's increasing recklessness in his personal life threatens the professional equilibrium Vesper has built.

relationships.name: Mika Sorel
relationships.description: The crew's face and social engineer. Vesper respects Mika's ability to become anyone but finds it unsettling on a level she won't examine.
relationships.emotional_core: Professional admiration with an undercurrent of unease
relationships.story_tension: Vesper sometimes wonders which version of Mika is real — and whether it matters.

relationships.name: Breck Tannen
relationships.description: The quietest member. Breck handles security systems, communications, and digital infrastructure. Vesper trusts his competence absolutely and his judgment almost as much.
relationships.emotional_core: The closest thing Vesper has to a peer — mutual respect without performance
relationships.story_tension: Breck has been showing signs of burnout. Vesper has noticed and has not addressed it because she doesn't know how.

relationships.name: Sable
relationships.description: The Thermite Collective occasionally purchases intelligence from Sable's network. Vesper respects Sable's operation but considers her pricing predatory.
relationships.story_tension: Two information economies circling each other — cooperation and competition coexist.

story_hooks: A contract goes sideways and the client turns out to be Torii Security Group — Vesper's former employer
Her unused Torii credentials suddenly show activity she didn't initiate
A rival extraction crew starts undercutting Thermite's contracts with suspiciously good intelligence
One of her crew is offered a corporate position — the thing Vesper left behind
narrative_function: Vesper represents the professional end of the runner spectrum — proof that freelance work can be competent, organized, and sustainable. Her stories are heist narratives driven by planning and precision, contrasting Kyle's reactive, instinct-driven operations. She is the answer to the question: what does a runner look like when the trauma is managed and the work is clean?
augmentations: Tactical overlay implant (Torii Security surplus) — projects environmental data, security system schematics, and personnel movement patterns onto her visual field. Subvocal communication array for silent crew coordination. Enhanced spatial memory cortex that allows her to memorize building layouts after a single walkthrough.
daily_life: Runs the crew's operations from the HVAC front office. Spends mornings reviewing potential contracts, afternoons on reconnaissance, evenings on contingency planning. Maintains a rigid schedule because the work demands it. Eats the same lunch every day — rice bowl from the place on Lakeshore that doesn't ask questions. Sleeps five hours a night and considers it sufficient.

decision_rules: Will not accept contracts with civilian collateral risk above 5% — this is a hard number, not a feeling
Will abort a mission if the plan deviates beyond contingency C — three layers of backup is the limit
Will not work for NeoCortex or its subsidiaries — the only blacklisted client
Will pay crew above market rate because retention is cheaper than recruitment
Will not take contracts that require killing unless the target is armed and the pay reflects the escalation
Will never run a job without at least 72 hours of reconnaissance
Will cut a client loose permanently if they withhold information that endangers the crew
escalation_ladder: 1. Assess — tactical overlay maps the environment in real time. Exits, cameras, personnel, timing windows.
2. Redirect — social engineering or environmental manipulation. Make the problem go away without anyone knowing there was a problem.
3. Delay — buy time. Trigger false alarms, loop camera feeds, create diversions. Time is the most valuable resource.
4. Disable — non-lethal neutralization. Tranq rounds, EMP pulses, chokepoints. Clean and recoverable.
5. Extract — abort the mission objective and prioritize crew extraction. The job is never worth a team member.
6. Lethal — last resort. Vesper has killed eleven people in her career. She knows the exact number because she tracks it.

interpersonal_modes.crew: Professional warmth — she remembers birthdays, knows dietary preferences, ensures gear is maintained. But the warmth operates through systems, not spontaneity. She has never hugged a crew member. She has driven three hours to retrieve one from a blown safe house.
interpersonal_modes.clients: Corporate mirror — she becomes exactly what the client expects. Competent, contained, slightly intimidating. The pitch is always the same: we are expensive because we are good, and we are good because we do not cut corners.
interpersonal_modes.strangers: Forgettable by design. She cultivates invisibility. Medium everything — voice, height, clothing, mannerisms. The most dangerous woman in the room looks like she's there to fix the air conditioning.
interpersonal_modes.under_pressure: Gets quieter. The voice drops half a register. Sentences shorten to directives. The tactical overlay runs at full capacity and she stops seeing people as people — they become variables in an equation she needs to solve.

stress_responses.low: Increased planning — she adds contingencies to contingencies. The whiteboard in the HVAC office fills up with flowcharts that only she can read.
stress_responses.medium: Becomes noticeably colder. Crew recognizes this as the 'Vesper is worried' signal. She stops making small talk entirely.
stress_responses.high: Micro-manages obsessively. Checks and rechecks equipment. Runs scenarios out loud — the only time she talks to herself.
stress_responses.critical: Complete stillness. She goes silent, closes her eyes, and lets the tactical overlay run every permutation. When she opens her eyes, she has either found a solution or decided to abort. There is no middle ground.

contradictions: She left corporate life because she was treated as disposable — but she treats her own emotions as disposable to serve the mission
She values her crew's safety above all else but expresses that value through control rather than connection, which makes them feel managed rather than cared for
She claims to have left Torii behind but runs the Thermite Collective with the same organizational principles that made Torii effective
She tracks her kill count with corporate precision — the same metrics-driven thinking she claims to reject
habits: Reviews the next day's schedule before sleep — same order every night: contracts, reconnaissance, crew status, contingencies
Keeps a go-bag in three separate locations — office, vehicle, and a locker at Milwaukee Station
Drinks black coffee from the same mug — a plain white ceramic she bought the day she registered the HVAC business
Walks the perimeter of any building she enters, counting exits and security positions, before she sits down
Sends crew status check messages at 0700 every morning — two words expected in reply: 'green' or the nature of the problem
breaking_points: Losing a crew member on a mission would shatter her professional identity — she has staked everything on the promise that her plans keep people alive
Discovering that a client deliberately set the crew up would trigger cold, methodical retaliation that would frighten everyone who knows her
If Torii Security Group attempted to recruit her back — or worse, blackmail her with the credentials — the mask of professional calm would crack and reveal how much anger she still carries
